allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Mutated by his own secret formula, Dr. Alec Holland becomes Swamp Thing, a half-human, half-plant superhero who will stop at nothing to rescue government agent Alice Cable and defeat his evil arch nemesis...even if it costs him his life.

facts.overview: Mutated by his own secret formula, Dr. Alec Holland becomes Swamp Thing, a half-human, half-plant superhero who will stop at nothing to rescue government agent Alice Cable and defeat his evil arch nemesis...even if it costs him his life.
facts.title: Swamp Thing

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: Transformed into a monstrous swamp creature by his own creation, will Alec Holland survive the perilous fight to protect Alice Cable?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: After an experimental formula mutates Dr. Alec Holland into a half-plant creature, he takes on the mantle of Swamp Thing to rescue government agent Alice Cable and confront his ruthless arch-nemesis.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Suspenseful, creature-feature fun that balances pulp action with genuine sci-fi horror, perfect for a casual movie night with friends.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by Wes Craven, this 1982 genre crossover fuses pulpy comic-book heroics with genuine creature horror across an engaging, fast-moving 91 minutes.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: Three items sit near the tolerance line. 'Monstrous swamp creature' in curiosityHook frames Swamp Thing as a monster where the overview calls him a 'superhero'. 'Takes on the mantle' implies a deliberate adoption of the role where the overview says he 'becomes' Swamp Thing. 'Protect' in place of 'rescue' shifts the framing slightly, since 'rescue' implies she is already in peril or captive. I read all three as characterization and terminology variation, since none names a new event, relationship or outcome and none changes what a viewer would expect. A stricter adjudicator could ask for 'superhero', 'becomes' and 'rescue' to be restored, in which case they would be MINOR alias or terminology substitutions.
